title: State the LDPC decoder numerical contract with its batch clauses
description:
Publishes the floating-point numerical contract of the LDPC min-sum decoder as one permanent reference page, with the clauses a multi-frame decoder adds, so each later kernel and entry point is reviewed against a single statement.

## Background

The canonical decoder is `LdpcDecoder` in `gf2-coding`: an f32 flooding decoder of the min-sum family over the canonical `EdgeLayout`, whose check update is the shared reduction `min_sum_check_row` and which stops a frame at the first iteration whose syndrome passes. Its numerical rules are stated in the rustdoc of `min_sum_check_row` and in the development record `dev/active/f63a2464/numerical-contract-review.md`; no permanent page owns them. An inter-frame decoder places the same message position of eight independent frames in the eight f32 lanes of one AVX2 register. A lane is a frame, so no reduction inside a check and no accumulation inside a variable is reassociated, and each frame's result equals the single-frame decoder's bit for bit. The bounded evaluation recorded in `dev/active/f63a2464/decision-record.md` selects no quantized, layered or QC-aware candidate, so the float flooding contract is the only decoder contract. Code claims the page rests on are in `dev/active/ed3d490e-zen3-ldpc-frame-simd/survey/source-evidence.json`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `docs/reference/ldpc-decoder-numerical-contract.md` states, for the f32 flooding min-sum family, the sign rule on signed zero and NaN, the tie rule of the two smallest magnitudes, the scaling of each min-sum rule, the absence of channel scaling and of saturation inside the decoder, the hard-decision rule, the variable-node accumulation order and the per-frame termination rule, each in agreement with the canonical decoder's source.
- [hard] REQ-02: The page states that punctured, truncated and filler positions reach the decoder as ordinary mother-code LLRs prepared by the rate-matching layer: the zero LLR for an untransmitted position and the finite filler magnitude for a filler position.
- [hard] REQ-03: The page states the batch clauses: a lane carries one frame; a frame's posterior LLR bit patterns, hard decisions, iteration count and convergence flags equal the single-frame decoder's on the same input for each batch size and lane position; a terminated or idle lane is not written again and changes no other lane; an idle lane holds zero LLRs.
- [hard] REQ-04: The page states that the supported LLR precision is f32, that sum-product frames take the single-frame decoder, and that quantized alphabets and layered schedules are outside the contract.
- [hard] REQ-05: The page is linked from the documentation index, and the rustdoc of `min_sum_check_row` cites it for the clauses the page owns in place of a second copy.

## Notes

The page addresses researchers: present tense, no measured figure, no account of how the contract was reached.

planning.outcome: The float decoder contract with its lane clauses has one permanent statement

terminal.consumer_family: readers of the decoder numerical contract
terminal.test_boundary: documentation mechanical checks on the reference page
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One reference page restates rules the source evidence ledger already locates

title: Provide the portable lane kernels of the min-sum decoder
description:
Adds to `gf2-kernels-simd` the eight-lane f32 type, the kernel function bundle of the inter-frame check and variable steps, a safe portable implementation of the bundle, and the behavioural suite each backend of the bundle runs.

## Background

The canonical decoder is `LdpcDecoder` in `gf2-coding`: an f32 flooding decoder of the min-sum family over the canonical `EdgeLayout`, whose check update is the shared reduction `min_sum_check_row` and which stops a frame at the first iteration whose syndrome passes. An inter-frame decoder places the same message position of eight independent frames in the eight f32 lanes of one AVX2 register. A lane is a frame, so no reduction inside a check and no accumulation inside a variable is reassociated, and each frame's result equals the single-frame decoder's bit for bit. The lane arrays are indexed by canonical edge id and then by lane for the two message directions, and by variable and then by lane for channel LLRs and beliefs; hard decisions are one byte per variable whose bit $l$ is the decision of lane $l$. `gf2-kernels-simd` holds the scalar reference of a kernel beside its vector form and does not depend on `gf2-coding`, so the kernels take plain slices: lane arrays, the check and variable prefix offsets and the slot-to-edge map of the canonical layout. The numerical rules are those of `docs/reference/ldpc-decoder-numerical-contract.md`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A public module of `gf2-kernels-simd` defines an eight-lane f32 type aligned to 32 bytes and a function bundle holding a check step for the plain, normalized and offset min-sum rules and a variable step that takes an active-lane mask, both over the lane arrays and canonical layout slices.
- [hard] REQ-02: A safe portable implementation of the bundle reproduces, in each lane, the bit patterns of `min_sum_check_row` and of the canonical variable step, including on signed zeros, NaN of either sign, infinities, finite extrema, equal smallest magnitudes, and checks of degree zero, one, two and at least nineteen.
- [hard] REQ-03: The variable step leaves the belief, the outgoing messages and the hard-decision bit of each inactive lane unchanged, and writes each active lane as the canonical step does.
- [hard] REQ-04: The behavioural assertions are one function of a bundle, so a later backend runs the identical assertions; they run on the portable bundle on any host.
- [hard] REQ-05: The module contains no `unsafe`, and its rustdoc states purpose, the panics on inconsistent slice lengths and the linear complexity in the edge count.

## Notes

The existing horizontal kernel `minsum_fn` reduces one slice and takes the IEEE sign bit in its vector lanes; the lane kernels do not call it.

planning.outcome: Lane kernel bundle with a portable implementation that follows the float contract

terminal.test_boundary: kernel behavioural suite over the portable bundle
terminal.worker_sized_reason: Two safe loops with one test function in a single new module

title: Carry decoder selectors in the coding tuning section
description:
Extends the coding-owned tuning section with a decode selector family and the typed route decision that reads it, so batch decoding takes each route from one calibrated source.

## Background

Selector values of `gf2-coding` live in its tuning section, resolved through the process-wide authority of `gf2_core::tuning`; the section holds the batch-encoding family, whose conservative values select the scalar reference. A batch decoder chooses between decoding frames one at a time and decoding a wave of eight frames in lanes, and partitions waves across workers; those three choices are selectors. The section keeps one wire identity and one owner codec.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The coding tuning section exposes a validated decode selector family: `lane_min_frames`, the smallest number of occupied lanes at which a wave takes the lane route; `lane_max_edges`, the largest Tanner-graph edge count that takes the lane route; and `granules_per_task`, the number of preferred-granularity frame groups one parallel task decodes.
- [hard] REQ-02: The conservative family routes each frame to the single-frame decoder and gives one group per task; each conservative value has one definition beside the route decision, re-exported by the tuning module.
- [hard] REQ-03: A typed route decision maps the occupied lanes of a wave, the edge count, the decoder algorithm and the lane capability to the single-frame route or the lane route, reads no value outside the selector family, and is tested on both sides of each selector.
- [hard] REQ-04: The owner codec encodes and decodes the family with per-field presence, reads a body without the family as the conservative family, rejects a null or unknown field and a zero `granules_per_task`, and decodes a committed profile that holds the encode family alone to the section it decoded to before.
- [hard] REQ-05: The section's wire identity is unchanged, the process-wide accessor resolves both families through one lookup, and the fresh-process tests observe the conservative family before installation and an installed family after it.
- [hard] REQ-06: The permanent pages that show how a coding section is built describe the two families in the present tense.

## Notes

title: Define the batch soft-decoder trait with its shared contract
description:
Adds to `gf2-coding` a batch soft-decoder trait beside `SoftDecoder` and `IterativeSoftDecoder`, default batch decoding for the existing soft decoders, and the behavioural contract function each implementer runs.

## Background

`gf2-coding` has two single-frame soft-decoding entry points: `SoftDecoder::decode_soft_with_result`, by shared reference, and `IterativeSoftDecoder::decode_iterative`, by mutable reference with an iteration cap. Its implementers are the OSD, ORBGRAND, GLDPC, LDPC and rate-matched 5G NR decoders. No trait decodes several frames in one call: the LDPC decoder has inherent batch functions, and each `gf2-sim` decode stage loops over frames itself. The modem layer has batch traits, `BatchMapper` and `BatchSoftDemapper`, that write into caller-provided storage and are usable boxed; the traits module carries shared contract functions such as `block_encoder_contract` that an implementer's tests call. A `gf2-sim` stage processes by shared reference with a default-constructed mutable scratch, so a batch decoder with a workspace is a value a stage builds once per scratch and calls mutably. The per-frame outcome type `DecodeOutcome` is LDPC-local. Code claims are in `dev/active/ed3d490e-zen3-ldpc-frame-simd/survey/source-evidence.json`, topics `decoder-traits`, `implementers`, `batch-trait-style` and `stage-boundary`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A public trait in `crates/gf2-coding/src/traits.rs` decodes a slice of LLR frames, each viewable as `[Llr]`, into caller-provided decoded words and per-frame outcomes in input order, by mutable reference, and reports the frame length, the decoded word length and the implementer's preferred batch granularity.
- [hard] REQ-02: The per-frame outcome type lives in the traits module, carries iteration count, convergence flag, syndrome flag and the optional query count of `DecoderResult`, and is the one outcome type of the crate; the LDPC module re-exports it.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each `SoftDecoder` is a batch decoder of granularity one through a default per-frame loop over `decode_soft_with_result`, and an adapter holding an iteration cap makes each `IterativeSoftDecoder` a batch decoder through `decode_iterative`.
- [hard] REQ-04: The trait's contract requires no steady-state allocation of an implementer; the default paths allocate only what the single-frame decode they call allocates, and the rustdoc says so.
- [hard] REQ-05: One public contract function takes a batch decoder, its single-frame reference and a frame set, and asserts input order, per-frame decoded words and outcomes equal to the reference, an empty batch, batch sizes below, at and above the implementer's granularity, an incomplete final group, and a frame set mixing early, late and non-converging frames.
- [hard] REQ-06: The contract function runs over the OSD, ORBGRAND, GLDPC, LDPC and rate-matched 5G NR decoders through the default paths.
- [hard] REQ-07: A test asserts that the default per-frame path of the LDPC and GLDPC decoders returns the hard decisions of the input LLRs with no iteration, and differs from the adapter's iterative result on a frame that needs decoding.
- [hard] REQ-08: Rustdoc states the trait's scope in the present tense: soft-decision block decoding of whole frames; hard-decision decoders, streaming decoders and batch encoding have their own entry points. It states panics on a wrong frame length and on mismatched output slices, and whether the trait is usable as a trait object.

## Notes

title: Decode LDPC frame batches in lanes behind the batch decoder trait
description:
Adds to `gf2-coding` the LDPC implementer of the batch soft-decoder trait: a decoder that owns a lane workspace, decodes frames in fixed waves of eight with per-frame termination, and returns each frame's result in input order.

## Background

The canonical decoder is `LdpcDecoder` in `gf2-coding`: an f32 flooding decoder of the min-sum family over the canonical `EdgeLayout`, whose check update is the shared reduction `min_sum_check_row` and which stops a frame at the first iteration whose syndrome passes. A lane is a frame, so no reduction inside a check and no accumulation inside a variable is reassociated, and each frame's result equals the single-frame decoder's bit for bit. `gf2-coding` has a batch soft-decoder trait with a shared contract function, `gf2-kernels-simd` provides the lane kernel bundle with a portable implementation, and the coding tuning section provides the decode selectors and the typed route decision. A wave is fixed: it runs until each of its lanes has terminated or the iteration cap is reached; a frame terminates as the single-frame decoder does, and a terminated lane is frozen by the kernel's active-lane mask. - [hard] REQ-06: A decoder built with explicit selectors takes the route those selectors give, and the default constructor reads the process-wide coding section once at construction.
- [hard] REQ-07: Rustdoc states purpose and panics, reports the workspace size in bytes through an accessor, and carries one example of the batch workflow through the trait.

title: Assert LDPC batch decoding at the posterior level across codes
description:
Adds the LDPC behavioural suite that holds each route of the LDPC batch decoder to the single-frame decoder at the posterior level, over standard codes, difficult inputs and each batch-size boundary.

## Background

The canonical decoder is `LdpcDecoder` in `gf2-coding`: an f32 flooding decoder of the min-sum family over the canonical `EdgeLayout`, whose check update is the shared reduction `min_sum_check_row` and which stops a frame at the first iteration whose syndrome passes. The batch soft-decoder trait of `gf2-coding` decodes a batch of LLR frames into caller-provided decoded words and per-frame outcomes in input order. Its LDPC implementer, the LDPC batch decoder, decodes fixed waves of eight lanes with per-frame termination, routes a wave to the lane kernels or to the single-frame decoder by the decode selectors of the coding tuning section, and returns each frame's result equal to the single-frame decoder's bit for bit as `docs/reference/ldpc-decoder-numerical-contract.md` states. The shared contract function of the trait asserts decoded words and outcomes; the LDPC claim is stronger, equal posterior bit patterns, and lane masking is where it can fail: a lane that terminates early, an idle lane or a frame that never converges must leave the other frames of its wave untouched. The suite covers codes of the DVB-T2 [Etsi2015] and 5G NR [ThreeGpp2017] standards.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One suite function takes the route under test and asserts, per frame, equal posterior LLR bit patterns, hard decisions, iteration counts and convergence flags against the single-frame decoder, for the three min-sum rules and both early-termination settings.
- [hard] REQ-02: The suite covers a DVB-T2 short code, 5G NR mother codes of both base graphs at three lifting sizes, and hand-built codes with checks of degree one, two and at least nine.
- [hard] REQ-03: Inputs include random codewords and the all-zero codeword through seeded noise at operating points where frames of one wave converge early, converge late and reach the iteration cap, frames holding signed zeros, saturated and extreme finite LLRs, NaN and infinite LLRs, and 5G NR frames with punctured and filler positions prepared by the rate-matching layer.
- [hard] REQ-04: Batch sizes 0, 1, 7, 8, 9, 15, 16 and 17 pass, a permutation of the input frames permutes the results identically, and replacing the other frames of a wave with non-converging frames leaves a frame's result unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-05: Each test meets the fast-tier budget; a case that cannot carries a descriptive slow-tier ignore reason.

## Notes

The suite asserts observable results only and does not read the lane workspace.

Source references: [Etsi2015], [ThreeGpp2017].

planning.outcome: Posterior-level suite holds each LDPC batch route to the single-frame decoder

title: Decode batches across workers through one pooled batch decoder
description:

title: Decode DVB-T2 concatenated frame batches in lanes
description:
